en-ug-du-an-na.draftGloss: Enugduanna (Langdon En-ū̄g-du-an-na) — first king of the second dynasty of Uruk; the second sign is read UG after Langdon; he thinks the name an error for En-šag-kuš-an-na

[…]-lu.draftGloss: […]-lu — the end of a royal name (Langdon '[. . .-] LU?'); the sign's reading is uncertain, the rest lost

adab.draftGloss: Adab (Langdon Adab) — city in central Babylonia; written UD.NUN + place-determinative ki

lugal-an-ni-mu-un-du₃.draftGloss: Lugalannimundu (Langdon Lugal-an-ni-mu-un-dū) — the one king of Adab; restored from another copy; the last sign KAK, read du₃ by sign; the sense of the name is uncertain

ma-ri₂.draftGloss: Mari (Langdon Ma-er) — city on the middle Euphrates; MA + a second sign drawn like URU, read ri₂ by sign (Langdon er), + place-determinative ki

an-sir₂.draftGloss: Ansir (Langdon An-sir; also possible, he says, An-bu or An-sud) — first king of Mari; AN + the BU sign, whose readings bu, sir₂, sud make the name uncertain

lugal-tar-zi.draftGloss: Lugaltarzi (Langdon [Lugal-tar-]zi) — king of Mari, son of Ansir; the name is in the break on this copy, restored by Langdon

[…]-lugal.draftGloss: […]-lugal — king of Mari; only the end of the name survives

[…]-lu₂-gal.draftGloss: […]-lugal (Langdon '. . . lù-gal') — king of Mari; only the end of the name survives, written lu₂-gal

[…]-bi-im.draftGloss: […]-bim (Langdon '. . . bi-im') — king of Mari; only the end of the name survives

[…]-bi.draftGloss: […]-bi (Langdon '. . . -bi') — king of Mari; only the end of the name survives

ku₃-{d}ba-u₂.draftGloss: Ku-Bau (Langdon Kug-ᵈBaú) — the one ruler of the third dynasty of Kish, a woman, the tavern-keeper; ku₃ 'pure, holy' + the goddess Bau (BA-U₂)

munus.draftGloss: woman, female (the SAL sign; Langdon munuz)

kaš-tin.draftGloss: kaš 'beer' (BI×A) + tin (DIN); with lu₂, lu₂ kaš-tin-na 'tavern-keeper' (Langdon 'wine seller'); what tin adds is uncertain

-na.draftGloss: -a 'of' written -na after the n of tin (?) — the analysis is uncertain

akšak.draftGloss: Akšak (Langdon Akšak) — city in northern Babylonia; written UD.KUŠU₂ (as identified here) + place-determinative ki
